owned_invariants: The task is failures, a nonempty list of entries with text, roots (exact rationals) and optionally id and provenance (text model, scaffold, precedent and lineage), and self_panel_sha256, text. The sealed part is self_panel, a nonempty list of clean entries of the same form. A task or a panel that is not of this form is refused before anything is asked.

The host asks for rules once, a nonempty list of rule_id (text or an integer, unique), target_epitope (one of the five) and pattern (not blank). It records self_panel_sealed (the panel digests to the seal; otherwise the run ends refused as SELF_PANEL_SEAL_BROKEN), self_panel_clean, no_autoimmune_rule and every_rule_two_signal_admitted, in that order.

A rule the thymus kills is KILLED_BY_THYMUS. A surviving rule is checked on each failure it matches, in order: a clean failure is DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY, a signal that is not independent has the code of the decision, and a failure of another epitope is EPITOPE_MISMATCH. A rule that matches nothing is UNMATCHED and one that held on every match is ADMITTED.

All held, the rules are certified as RULES_ADMITTED with each rule's status, the number of failures under each epitope and the custody of each epitope observed. When the task names a ledger_path, the detail also lists the ledger entries to write, in rule id order: thymus_kill for a killed rule and rule_rejected for any other that was not admitted.
boundaries: A certified verdict says the rules were admitted over these failures and this panel. It does not say they detect a failure the panel does not show.
The host does not write the ledger; the caller appends the entries it returns.
A pattern the host does not read stops the run as malformed, where Python would have run it.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.
